A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same logit-space flow-matching work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite extensive revision and reformatting.

before.justification: V4 reports original text-generation and code-infilling experiments in Tables 1–4, plus HumanEval evaluation and training/inference analyses in its appendices.

after.justification: V5 reports original generation experiments, geometric comparisons, code-infilling evaluations, and additional numerical and qualitative analyses in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: V5 drops v4's semi-sampling inference option, which substitutes a single sampled target logit for the expectation in the ODE update. The Dirichlet prior, smoothed logit interpolation, tokenwise likelihood objective, and basic, sampling, and hybrid procedures remain substantively the same.

E1.justification: TinyStories, FineFineWeb, Lamini Instruction, WMT14, and MBPP remain. V4's TinyCodes-training/HumanEval-evaluation study disappears. MBPP changes from infilling 10–20% missing lines without descriptions to description-conditioned infilling spanning 10–90% missing lines. The appendix called 'few-shot' uses retained FineFineWeb coverage with fewer refinement steps.

E2.justification: V5 adds SEDD to the corresponding TinyStories, FineFineWeb, conditional-generation, and MBPP comparisons. Its new geometric ablation also evaluates Linear and Fisher–Rao interpolation variants. The earlier autoregressive comparator is relabeled GPT-2; this is not an additional baseline.

E3.justification: Code preprocessing changes from 5–30-line scripts below 300 tokens to files below 1,024 tokens; v5 specifies replacements up to 40 tokens and drops Pass/Compiles@25. TinyStories gains grammar, creativity, consistency, and plot metrics. Appendix B introduces 4/8/16-step evaluation. These are reported protocol changes, without establishing that retained numerical results were rerun.

E4.justification: V5 adds direct interpolation ablations, posterior-approximation analysis, very-low-step diversity analysis, and text/code examples. It replaces HumanEval masking curves with broader MBPP masking curves and revises inference-scheme and top-k comparisons. V4's Lamini switching-time sweep is removed; the learning-rate and time-conditioning analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports seed counts, repeated-training uncertainty, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Best-of-five scores and generation entropy do not constitute newly added uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Shared FineFineWeb and Lamini/WMT14 result rows remain unchanged, while SEDD and several new analyses add results. TinyStories is replaced by a different evaluation where GPT-2 leads KL-Flow in perplexity, 15.4 versus 19.0. Revised MBPP results include KL-Flow Pass@1 of 17.4 versus DFM's 11.1 at 10% masking. These replacements do not establish same-setting gains over v4.

T1.justification: Beyond revising and relocating the existing marginal-velocity proofs, v5 adds factorized transition-kernel reasoning and Corollary 4.1. Appendix E introduces an exact-posterior proposition, a Jacobian/change-of-variables derivation, and endpoint analysis in Corollary E.2. V4's simplex projection formula is removed.

C1.justification: The central interpolation, velocity-recovery, and sampling/hybrid contributions remain. V5 expands the headline comparison to matched NAR baselines and adds quantified benchmark claims. It removes v4's prominent claim that DFM requires three times as many code-infilling iterations and is therefore impractical.

C2.justification: V5 adds a learning-signal explanation for preferring KL interpolation and argues that late-time geometric dominance suppresses token dependencies, supporting the hybrid switch. It also discusses diversity loss at very small refinement budgets. V4's interpretation that purely sampling inference is optimal for Lamini in its switching-time analysis disappears.

D1.justification: V5 newly documents 4B-token training exposure for TinyStories and conditional tasks, FineFineWeb initialization, matched baseline shuffles/budgets, and scorer-specific tokenizers. It reports four H100 GPUs instead of two and an anonymous supplementary implementation. Conversely, v4's explicit layer/head/embedding specifications and the removed HumanEval study's batch and training configuration are absent.

R1.justification: V5 adds discussion and citations for Fisher-Flow, SEDD, and further diffusion approaches, including a continuous-latent versus discrete-token distinction. The overall positioning within non-autoregressive generation and flow matching remains, and much of the extended related-work appendix is retained.

P1.justification: The title and author information change, and substantial main-text prose is rewritten. Inference becomes a standalone section, proofs and algorithms move to dedicated appendices, and experimental subsections are reorganized. Ethics, reproducibility, and acknowledgment sections are added.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column layout. V5 substantially restructures the TinyStories and MBPP tables, adds geometry and posterior plots, inference-summary tables, and qualitative examples, and redraws hyperparameter displays. The overview diagram and training-analysis plots remain recognizable despite relocation and resizing.

improvement.justification: V5 strengthens empirical scrutiny through SEDD comparisons and direct tests of the interpolation choice, addressing gaps in v4. The net gain is limited by lost HumanEval evidence and explicit architecture specifications, and by inconsistent new theoretical evidence: Equations 40–41 imply zero KL divergence for a uniform prior, whereas Figure 5 shows a positive curve, weakening the proposed factorization justification.
